activities.name: Trinity College Long Room & Book of Kells Tour
activities.description: You will step inside the magnificent 18th-century Old Library to stand beneath the barrel-vaulted ceiling of the Long Room, surrounded by 200,000 of the world's oldest books. Afterward, you will view the meticulously detailed 9th-century Book of Kells, marveling at the vibrant Celtic illumination preserved through the ages.
activities.duration_note: Advance online booking is mandatory. Peak times sell out weeks ahead.

activities.name: Guinness Storehouse Gravity Bar Connoisseur Experience
activities.description: You will journey through the seven-floor industrial storehouse to learn the intricate craft of brewing Ireland's famous stout. The experience culminates in an exclusive, private tasting lounge where a master bartender guides you through four distinct Guinness variants before you head to the panoramic Gravity Bar for your perfect pint.
activities.duration_note: Includes multiple premium tastings and a souvenir glass. Adults only for this specific package.

activities.name: Traditional Irish Music Session at The Cobblestone Pub
activities.description: You will squeeze into this historic, unpretentious pub in Smithfield, renowned as Dublin's premier home for authentic traditional music. Sitting amongst locals, you will sip a finely poured stout while witnessing world-class fiddlers, uilleann pipers, and tin whistlers engage in an organic, lively musical session.
activities.duration_note: No cover charge, cost is for drinks. Arrive before 7:00 PM to secure a seat near the musicians.

activities.name: Brú na Bóinne Neolithic Passage Tomb Guided Exploration
activities.description: You will journey into the Boyne Valley to stand before Newgrange, a massive prehistoric monument older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids. Guided by an archaeologist, you will walk down the narrow stone passage to the central chamber and discover how ancient engineers perfectly aligned the roof box to illuminate the room during the winter solstice.
activities.duration_note: Requires deep advance booking. Access inside the chamber is strictly limited to official guided groups.

activities.name: Howth Head Coastal Cliff Hike & Harbor Walk
activities.description: You will navigate the rugged peninsula paths high above Dublin Bay, taking in crashing waves, sea caves, and the iconic Baily Lighthouse. After tackling the windswept dirt trails, you will descend into the fishing village where wild seals often gather near the piers waiting for scraps.
activities.duration_note: Free public trail. Requires sturdy hiking shoes; trails can be muddy and slick in wind or rain.

activities.name: Glendalough Monastic Valley & Upper Lake Hike
activities.description: You will wander through the serene 'Valley of the Two Lakes' to explore a beautifully preserved 6th-century monastic settlement, including its famous stone Round Tower. From there, you can choose between a peaceful lakeside stroll or a steep timber-step climb up the Spinc trail for panoramic views of the glacial valley.
activities.duration_note: The valley is free to access; the price accounts for the parking fee at the Upper Lake lot.

activities.name: Sea Kayaking with Seals around Dalkey Island
activities.description: You will launch your kayak from Coliemore Harbour and paddle across the sound to a historic, uninhabited island. Along the way, a colony of inquisitive resident harbor seals will swim alongside your boat, and you will land on the island to explore its historic Martello tower.
activities.duration_note: Operates April through October. Wet suits and safety gear are fully provided by instructors.

activities.name: Historical Walking Tour of Dublin Castle & Kilmainham Gaol
activities.description: You will join an expert historian to chart Ireland's turbulent past, beginning at the medieval courtyard of Dublin Castle, the former seat of British rule. You will then transition to the bleak stone corridors of Kilmainham Gaol, where the leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were held and executed.
activities.duration_note: Gaol tickets must be booked online exactly 28 days in advance when released, as they sell out immediately.

activities.name: Gap of Dunloe Boat and Pony Trap Expedition
activities.description: You will embark on an old-school Irish adventure, starting with an open-topped wooden boat cruise across Killarney's three pristine lakes. Upon landing at Brandon's Cottage, you will hop into a traditional horse-drawn pony trap—or rent a rugged hybrid bicycle—to traverse the narrow, towering mountain pass of the Gap of Dunloe.
activities.duration_note: Highly weather dependent. Operates primarily from April to October; dress in warm layers.

activities.name: Skellig Michael Eco-Boat Cruise & Monastic Island Landing
activities.description: You will cross the rough Atlantic waters to a jagged, UNESCO-protected rock rising sharply out of the ocean. If you secure a rare landing permit, you will climb over 600 hand-carved, 6th-century stone steps into the clouds to wander among ancient beehive monastic huts and thousands of nesting Atlantic puffins.
activities.duration_note: Extremely strict seasonal window (May-Sept). High physical fitness required; vertigo sufferers should avoid landing.

activities.name: West Cork Seafood Tasting at The Fishy Fishy Restaurant
activities.description: You will secure a table at Chef Martin Shanahan's legendary culinary haven in Ireland's gourmet capital. You will indulge in a feast of pan-fried organic salmon, dynamic local lobster, or fresh-caught Dublin Bay prawns sourced directly from the fishermen unloading their catch at the harbor just yards away.
activities.duration_note: Dinner reservations are essential on weekends. Closed during the depth of winter (Jan-Feb).

activities.name: Craft Snug Tasting & Live Trad at Dick Mack's Pub
activities.description: You will step through the doors of an iconic dual-purpose institution that is part traditional haberdashery/cobbler and part family-run pub. You will pull up a stool in a cozy wooden 'snug' room, sample a flight of whiskies or bespoke beers brewed on-site, and lose yourself in a nightly traditional music session.
activities.duration_note: Fills up incredibly fast during summer months; arrive early evening to get inside the main bar area.

activities.name: Blarney Castle & Poison Garden Exploration
activities.description: You will climb the narrow, winding stone stairs of this historic 15th-century stronghold to lean backward over the parapet and kiss the famous Blarney Stone to claim the 'gift of eloquence.' Afterward, you will stroll through the beautifully manicured grounds to find the enclosed Poison Garden, filled with dangerous, legendary botanical specimens like wolfsbane and mandrake.
activities.duration_note: Lines for the stone can exceed an hour in mid-summer; visit first thing in the morning to beat the tour buses.

activities.name: Atlantic Coast Surfing on Brandon Bay
activities.description: You will suit up in heavy-duty neoprene and hit the long, sandy stretches of the Maharees peninsula, exposed to the full, clean swell of the Atlantic Ocean. Under the guidance of local ISA-certified instructors, you will learn to read the breaks and ride your first consistent green waves against a backdrop of dramatic mountains.
activities.duration_note: Ages 8 and up. All equipment (boards, winter wetsuits, booties) is included in the lesson fee.

activities.name: Thermal Spa Day at Sámas Spa
activities.description: You will retreat into a luxury wellness sanctuary carved directly into a wooded hillside overlooking Kenmare Bay. Your sensory experience includes an open-air tropical rain shower, a relaxing soak in an outdoor heated infinity pool suspended over the forest canopy, and a customized hot stone massage utilizing organic Irish seaweed blends.
activities.duration_note: Bespoke adult-only facility. Advance spa treatment reservations are mandatory.

activities.name: Ring of Kerry Scenic Driving Exploration
activities.description: You will navigate a legendary 179-kilometer loop that winds past dramatic coastal landscapes, emerald pastures, and historic stone villages. You will pull off at world-class lookout points like Ladies View and Moll's Gap to gaze down at the expansive Lakes of Killarney tucked within the mountains.
activities.location: Ring of Kerry Circuit, County Kerry
activities.duration_note: Free self-drive route. To avoid getting stuck behind tour buses, drive the loop clockwise.

activities.name: Cliffs of Moher Coastal Path Guided Trek
activities.description: You will skip the crowded main visitor center and embark on a thrilling, raw cliff-edge trek starting from Hag's Head. Walking along a narrow dirt trail with the salty sea spray on your face, you will watch the sheer stone face drop over 200 meters into the churning Atlantic Ocean below.
activities.location: Liscannor to Doolin Trail, County Clare
activities.duration_note: Requires strong footwear and focus; there are no safety barriers on this wild, unpaved local path.

activities.name: Aran Islands Exploration & Dún Aonghasa Bike Ride
activities.description: You will board a morning ferry to the largest of the Aran Islands, where Irish is still the spoken first language. You will rent a bicycle to pedal past endless maze-like stone walls before hiking up to Dún Aonghasa, a spectacular, semi-circular prehistoric hillfort built on the edge of a vertical 100-meter drop.
activities.location: Kilronan Pier, Inis Mór, Galway Bay
activities.duration_note: Ferry pricing includes the round-trip ticket from Rossaveel; bike rental on the island costs extra (~15-20 EUR).

activities.name: Galway Market Native Oyster & Chowder Feast
activities.description: You will weave through the bustling, narrow lanes of the historic weekend market beside St. Nicholas' Church. You will stand at an open-air seafood stall to sample premium, mineral-rich native Galway flat oysters shucked right in front of you, accompanied by a hot, comforting bowl of thick seafood chowder and buttered brown soda bread.
activities.duration_note: The market operates strictly on Saturdays (8am-6pm) and Sundays (12pm-6pm) all year round.

activities.name: Late Night Trad Session at The Crane Bar
activities.description: You will ascend the stairs of this iconic, green-fronted pub in Galway's West End, famous for its dedication to traditional arts. In the intimate upstairs room, you will grab a pint and witness an unfiltered gathering of musicians playing tin whistles, button accordions, and bodhráns in an acoustic setting.
activities.duration_note: Music starts nightly around 9:30 PM. Stand-room only is common, so get there early.

activities.name: Geological Exploration of The Burren Karst Landscape
activities.description: You will wander across a fascinating, moon-like plateau of grey limestone pavements fissured by deep cracks called grikes. You will discover an incredible ecosystem where arctic, alpine, and mediterranean wildflowers grow side-by-side, and visit the iconic 5,000-year-old Poulnabrone Dolmen tomb.
activities.location: The Burren National Park, County Clare
activities.duration_note: National park entry is free; price accounts for local guided walking tours or nearby cave entries.

activities.name: Sea Kayaking & Coastal Foraging in Killary Fjord
activities.description: You will paddle a stable sea kayak through the deep, glassy waters of Ireland's only true glacial fjord, framed by towering mountain peaks. Along the shoreline, your guide will show you how to identify and forage wild edible seaweeds and rock mussels clinging to the stone edges.
activities.duration_note: Operates April to October. Suitable for beginners; all specialized thermal and water safety gear is provided.

activities.name: Connemara Seaweed Bath Soak at Voya Seaweed Baths
activities.description: You will step into a private wood-paneled room to submerge yourself in a steaming bath of fresh, hand-harvested Atlantic bladderwrack seaweed. The hot water releases the weed's natural, mineral-rich oils, creating a deeply relaxing, therapeutic soak designed to detoxify the skin and soothe tired muscles after hiking.
activities.duration_note: Includes a private steam cabinet session prior to your bath. Advance reservation required.

activities.name: Sky Road Scenic Drive & Kylemore Abbey Viewpoint
activities.description: You will drive along a narrow, looping coastal road that climbs high above Clifden Bay, offering dramatic panoramic views of the rugged Atlantic coastline and offshore islands. The route leads deep into Connemara, concluding with a view of Kylemore Abbey's neo-Gothic granite facade reflecting perfectly in a dark lake.
activities.duration_note: The coastal drive is free; price is for entry tickets if you choose to go inside the Kylemore Abbey estate gardens.

activities.name: Big Wave Surf Watching & Reef Break Foiling
activities.description: You will stand on the rocky headland of Mullaghmore Head to watch professional tow-in surfers tackle world-famous, massive swells that can reach over 15 meters high. If you are an experienced ocean athlete, you can book a customized jet-ski assisted foil or tow session to ride the legendary Atlantic reef break.
activities.duration_note: Watching from land is free. Elite water activities are highly exclusive, seasonal, and require expert certification.

activities.name: Slieve League Pilgrim Path Mountain Ridge Hike
activities.description: You will scale the dramatic slopes of Slieve League to stand on some of the highest marine cliffs in Europe, dropping almost three times further than the Cliffs of Moher. Experienced hikers can cross 'One Man's Pass,' a narrow, exhilarating stone ridge with precipitous drops into the ocean on one side and a mountain lake on the other.
activities.duration_note: Price is for the shuttle bus from the visitor lot. The ridge walk can be dangerous in strong winds or thick Atlantic fog.

activities.name: Wild Foraged Dinner at Eala Bhán Restaurant
activities.description: You will dine along the banks of the Garavogue River in an upscale venue that weaves local history and poetry into its menu. You will experience a refined meal featuring locally sourced Sligo venison, wild garlic oil, and chanterelle mushrooms foraged directly from the foothills of nearby Benbulben mountain.
activities.duration_note: Reservations required. Request a riverside table for beautiful twilight views.

activities.name: Craft Beers and Live Music at The Strand Bar
activities.description: You will walk straight off the surf beach and step into a lively establishment that has been the beating heart of the local community for generations. You will find a spot next to one of the open turf fires, sample a pint of craft ale from Sligo's local breweries, and listen to regular live music sessions.
activities.duration_note: Incredibly popular on Sunday evenings when local musicians gather after the weekend surf sessions.

activities.name: Carrowmore Megalithic Cemetery Walking Tour
activities.description: You will walk among the largest and oldest collections of megalithic tombs in Ireland, dating back over 5,500 years. You will explore a sacred landscape of stone circles and passage cairns, perfectly framed by the striking flat-topped silhouette of Knocknarea mountain in the distance.
activities.duration_note: Operates seasonally from Easter through October. Most of the terrain is open grassland, so bring weather-proof clothing.

activities.name: Donegal Bay Waterbus Cruise & Seal Colony Island Tour
activities.description: You will step aboard a spacious, fully accessible catamaran that glides through the calm, scenic waters of Donegal Bay. As you sail past green outer islands, the captain will bring the vessel close to a natural seal colony where dozens of harbor seals lounge on the rocky shores.
activities.duration_note: Includes live commentary and a musical performance on the lower deck during the return trip.

activities.name: Strandhill Traditional Seaweed Bath & Steam Session
activities.description: You will unwind in a historic bathhouse situated right on the edge of a wild surf beach. You will enjoy a private steam session to open your pores before sinking into a heavy porcelain tub filled with warm, amber-colored seawater infused with organic, freshly harvested Irish kelp.
activities.duration_note: Advance booking is highly recommended on weekends when surfers fill the village.

activities.name: Gleniff Horseshoe Valley Glacial Drive
activities.description: You will drive down a quiet, spectacular single-track loop road nestled within a dramatic, glacier-carved mountain amphitheater. You will look up at the sheer limestone cliffs of Dartry mountain range and see Diarmuid and Gráinne's cave high up on the mountain face, linked to famous Irish mythological tales.
activities.duration_note: Free public driving or cycling loop. The road is very narrow; drive carefully and watch for wandering sheep.

activities.name: Lough Derg Wakeboarding & Water Ski Adventure
activities.description: You will suit up and hit the expansive waters of Ireland's third-largest lake, a beautiful freshwater playground cutting through the midlands. Towed behind a high-spec competition speed boat, you will cut across wake fields and learn carving techniques from professional local coaches against a backdrop of rolling hills.
activities.duration_note: Operates May through September. Includes all premium gear, impact vests, and wetsuits.

activities.name: Clonmacnoise Monastic City Guided Ancient Exploration
activities.description: You will explore the extensive stone ruins of a major 6th-century center of religion and learning, beautifully positioned on the banks of the River Shannon. You will walk among ancient stone churches, high crosses, and two historic round towers that survived countless Viking raids.
activities.duration_note: Includes access to an excellent indoor museum displaying the original, delicate 9th-century carved high stone crosses.

activities.name: Slow-Roasted Irish Lamb Feast at The Left Bank Bistro
activities.description: You will dine at a highly regarded midlands restaurant that champions ingredients harvested from the surrounding pastures and lakes. You will enjoy an exquisite meal featuring tender, slow-cooked line-caught Shannon basin lamb served with a rich rosemary jus and creamy gratin potatoes.
activities.duration_note: Booking advised for weekend evening dining slots.

activities.name: Historical Pints at Sean's Bar (Ireland's Oldest Pub)
activities.description: You will step onto sawdust-covered floors inside an officially certified establishment dating back to 900 AD. You will examine the ancient wattle-and-daub walls uncovered during renovations, chat with the bartender, and enjoy a premium Irish whiskey drink next to an open turf fire.
activities.duration_note: Regular live acoustic music acts perform every night of the week. No cover charge.

activities.name: Lough Key Forest Park Canopy Walk & Island Exploration
activities.description: You will wander through a majestic estate featuring historic trees and underground servant tunnels. You will navigate Ireland's only tree-top canopy walk, safely suspended 9 meters above the forest floor, offering beautiful bird's-eye views of the lake and Castle Island.
activities.duration_note: Park entry is free; price is for the specific multi-activity canopy and tunnel visitor experience pass.

activities.name: Canoeing the Ancient Ballyconnell Canal Trails
activities.description: You will paddle a traditional open canoe down peaceful, tree-lined waterways that connect the historic Shannon and Erne river systems. You will navigate ancient stone locks, spot local kingfishers darting along the banks, and pull into quiet lakeside villages for lunch.
activities.duration_note: Includes all boat rentals, paddles, and personal flotation devices. Perfect for families.

activities.name: Old Rail Trail Cycling Journey
activities.description: You will rent a touring bicycle and cycle along a beautifully flat, dedicated greenway path conversion of an old historic railway line. You will cruise past traditional midlands farmlands, old stone arched bridges, and historic, disused railway stations completely isolated from motor traffic.
activities.duration_note: Price accounts for full-day standard bicycle rental from local town hubs.

activities.name: Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge Thrill Crossing
activities.description: You will test your nerve by walking across a narrow rope bridge suspended 30 meters above rocks and crashing waves. Originally erected by salmon fishermen in 1755, the bridge links the high coastal cliffs to a tiny, rugged island, offering stunning views of the Scottish coastline on a clear day.
activities.duration_note: Strictly timed online tickets required. Closed during excessively high winds for passenger safety.

activities.name: Titanic Belfast Interactive Shipyard Experience
activities.description: You will explore the world's largest Titanic visitor experience, located on the exact slipway where the famous vessel was designed and launched. You will navigate multi-dimensional galleries featuring dark rides, interactive shipyard reconstructions, and underwater exploration footage detailing the ship's tragic history.
activities.duration_note: Pre-booking your dynamic entry time slot online is highly recommended to avoid long museum queues.

activities.name: Traditional Ulster Fry Breakfast at Maggie May's
activities.description: You will sit down at a beloved local diner to take on Northern Ireland's ultimate morning culinary tradition. Your plate will come loaded with premium local sausages, back bacon, fried eggs, black pudding, and the defining grilled elements: authentic griddled potato bread and soda farls.
activities.duration_note: No booking required; expect a lively crowd of locals and students on weekend mornings.

activities.name: Historic Snug Pints at The Crown Liquor Saloon
activities.description: You will step inside an exquisitely preserved Victorian palace featuring ornate carved mahogany booths, etched glass panels, and original gas lamps. You will close the door of your private wooden snug booth, use the vintage buzzer to request service, and enjoy a local craft ale or stout.
activities.duration_note: Owned by the National Trust; get there by mid-afternoon if you want to secure a private booth.

activities.name: Giant's Causeway Hexagonal Basalt Column Trail
activities.description: You will walk along the ocean's edge to climb across 40,000 interlocking volcanic basalt columns that step gradually into the Irish Sea. You will marvel at the uncanny symmetry of the stone pillars, formed by cooling lava 60 million years ago, or choose to believe local folklore of the giant Finn McCool.
activities.duration_note: The natural site is free to access on foot via public right-of-way; the fee applies to using the visitor center parking.

activities.name: Island Hopping Cruise across Lower Lough Erne
activities.description: You will board a waterbus from Enniskillen to cruise through a scenic maze of island waterways. The boat will land at Devenish Island, where you will step ashore to examine an expansive 6th-century monastic site featuring an incredibly complete 30-meter high stone Round Tower.
activities.duration_note: Operates daily from May to September; weekend-only sailings during the shoulder month of April.

activities.name: Belfast Political History Black Cab Guided Tour
activities.description: You will ride inside an iconic black taxi while a knowledgeable local driver guides you through the complex political history of Belfast. You will stop to examine the towering Peace Walls and the famous political murals of the Falls and Shankill roads, gaining raw insight into the period known as The Troubles.
activities.duration_note: Price is typically fixed per vehicle for up to 3-4 passengers, making it highly cost-effective for small groups.

activities.name: House of Waterford Crystal Master Blowers Tour
activities.description: You will step onto the active factory floor to witness the intense heat and incredible skill behind world-famous luxury glass making. You will watch master craftsmen transform molten crystal utilizing ancient blowing pipes, and see the meticulous hand-cutting process that defines premium Irish crystalware.
activities.duration_note: Includes access to the massive global retail gallery. Booking online secures your preferred tour time.

activities.name: Medieval Mile Walking Tour & Kilkenny Castle
activities.description: You will stroll down narrow, historic cobbled lanes connecting ancient stone merchant houses, historic slipways, and medieval churches. The highlight is entering Kilkenny Castle, a magnificent 12th-century fortress, where you will wander through the grand, tapestry-lined picture gallery.
activities.duration_note: Castle tickets can be purchased at the gate, but pre-booking ensures access during busy summer travel months.

activities.name: Traditional Waterford Blaa Breakfast Tasting
activities.description: You will visit a traditional local bakery to try Waterford's protected, historical bread roll—the Blaa. You will sink your teeth into a remarkably soft, flour-dusted yeast roll loaded with hot, crispy local back bacon or traditional cured Irish pork sausage links.
activities.duration_note: Blaas are traditionally eaten fresh in the morning; bakeries often run completely out by early afternoon.

activities.name: Artisanal Red Ale Craft Tasting at Smithwick's Experience
activities.description: You will tour the historic micro-brewing site built on the ruins of a 13th-century Franciscan abbey. After learning about the unique brewing process, your evening concludes in the tasting room where you will sample a flight of smooth, ruby-red Smithwick's ales.
activities.duration_note: Last brewery tour departs at 5:00 PM, making it an excellent start to your evening itinerary.

activities.name: Waterford Greenway Coastal Bike Ride
activities.description: You will rent a trail bicycle and ride along a spectacular 46-kilometer car-free pathway following an old historic railway line. You will pass over historic stone viaducts, cruise through a long, dark brick-lined tunnel, and enjoy stunning panoramic views of the dramatic Copper Coast beaches.
activities.duration_note: Price is for a standard hybrid bike rental. Local shuttle buses can bring you back to your starting hub.

activities.name: Wreck Diving & Sea Cave Kayaking along the Copper Coast
activities.description: You will explore the dramatic sea caves, hidden coves, and soaring red sandstone cliffs of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Guided by local marine experts, you will paddle into secluded caves or scuba dive among historic coastal shipwrecks hidden beneath the waves.
activities.duration_note: Operates strictly May-Sept. Participants should be comfortable swimming in open sea water conditions.
